sections.COMMENTS:
This Composite Source straddles the region between the Molise foothills and the Capitanata plain, across the high Fortore R. valley, and belongs to the oblique to right-lateral strike-slip system that affects the central and southern Adriatic foreland. This Source is a near-vertical, ca. N-dipping, fault to the east of the main extensional axis of the southern Apennines.
Historical and instrumental catalogues (Boschi et al., 2000; Gruppo di Lavoro CPTI, 2004; Pondrelli et al., 2006; Guidoboni et al., 2007) show a sparse intermediate to damaging seismicity in this region, including the 20 August 1941 (Mw 5.4, S. Severo) event that took place in the eastern sector of the area, while the 11 October 1125 (Mw 5.7, Sannio-Molise) event hit to the southwest. Most importantly, this region has been affected by the 30 July 1627 (Mw 6.7, Gargano) earthquake that has occurred in the eastern sector, while the western one was affected by the well known twin earthquakes of 31 October-1 November 2002 (both Mw 5.7, Molise).
This Source represents a deep E-W fault that can be seen as the western prolongation of the well known Mattinata Fault, active as deep as 25 km. Such evidence was shown by the activation of the sources that have caused the 2002 Molise earthquakes. This sequence has also shown that seismogenic faulting in this area is essentially blind, affecting only the deeper part of the seismogenic layer â€“ a fact that seems to characterize the entire seismogenic domain east of the southern Apennines backbone, and possibly of the central ones too. The eastern sector of this Source is thought to have caused the destructive 1627 earthquake. The activity of this latter sector is also shown by its control on both long-and short-term drainage pattern of the Fortore R. on its course toward the Adriatic Sea.
Three segments of this Source have been associated with key earthquakes that have affected this region. For an in-depth analysis of seismogenesis in this region, the reader can refer to the Individual Sources in this Database.
The strike of this source was based on that of the mapped structures. The dip was based on seismological data and geometrical considerations. The rake represents oblique, right-lateral strike slip, based on seismological data. The minimum and maximum depth were based on seismological and geological data. The slip rate was inferred from geodynamic considerations for the tectonic environment that includes this Source.
